title: Consuming a Doubled Input Bit
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $w,u$ be Boolean words, and choose a saved configuration of $M$ on input $w$, phase indices $q,q'\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, Boolean values $a,c,a',c',b$, a natural number $i$ with $i+2\le |w|$, integer offsets $j,j'$, and a sign $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ such that $j+d=j'$. Suppose the $i$-th input bit is $b$, and the evaluator's transition from semantic phase $q$ with bits $a,c$ and skip flag false, upon reading $b$ in the canonical configuration at offset $i$ and certificate-head offset $j$, is the administrative action that moves the input head right, moves the certificate head by $d$, emits nothing, and enters phase $q'$ with bits $a',c'$ and skip flag true. Then two evaluator steps from that canonical configuration reach the canonical configuration at input offset $i+2$, certificate-head offset $j'$, and phase $q'$ with bits $a',c'$ and skip flag false.
hypotheses_covered: finite Boolean machine $M$ with $k$ work tapes
the stated evaluator transition is the specified administrative action
replaced:
Suppose the evaluator's transition at a semantic state on the current input bit is
the administrative action moving right, displacing the certificate head by $d$, and
entering a new semantic state with the skip flag set. Then two machine steps — the
semantic transition followed by its silent skip — consume the doubled input bit:
the input position advances by two, the certificate head by $d$, and the control
reaches the new semantic state with the skip flag cleared. The certificate head
moves only on the first of the two physical transitions.
